headline: Demis Hassabis of Google DeepMind said recent AI hacking incidents are early warning shots of larger ones to come.
score_reason: Pool score kept: on-record warning from a leading AI scientist, carried by Reuters and several outlets; a forecast, not an event.
importance_line: Hassabis is one of the people building frontier AI, so his warning adds weight to calls for security rules, and it affects any organisation running AI agents, but the predicted larger incidents are his judgment, not a documented event.
summary: Reuters reports that Demis Hassabis, co-founder and chair of Google DeepMind and chief scientist of Google parent Alphabet, told an AI summit in Dublin that hacks by AI agents are "early warning shots" and could become major incidents within a year or two unless industry, companies and governments do more to secure these systems. He said an international standards body would eventually be needed but would have to build a certification process that is proportionate to risk and can change quickly.
notes: Reuters page needs login (401). Text read at The Hindu, which carries the Reuters report. Same Dublin conference: Microsoft president Brad Smith called 2026 a 'sobering year' and said AI safety laws are urgently needed.
